title: Heritage walk in Chennai: Fort St George, Mylapore and the Marina
seo_title: Heritage Walk in Chennai: Historical Places and Routes
meta_description: Plan a heritage walk in Chennai: Fort St George, George Town, Mylapore and Triplicane, the Government Museum, routes and advice for school groups.
summary: A heritage walk in Chennai usually covers Fort St George and George Town, where the English East India Company settled in 1640; the Marina and its Indo-Saracenic university buildings; and the older temple towns of Mylapore and Triplicane, whose temples are far older than the colonial city. The Government Museum at Egmore holds the Amaravati sculptures and Chola bronzes.

sections.h2: Why Chennai matters for Indian heritage
paras: Chennai (Madras) is a colonial city built around much older settlements. In 1639 to 1640 the English East India Company got a grant of land on the coast and built Fort St George, its first major fortified base in India. Around it grew Black Town (later George Town) for Indian merchants, weavers and dubashes (interpreters), and to the south lay the temple towns of Mylapore and Triplicane, both praised by Tamil devotional poets more than a thousand years earlier.

That mix lets a single morning move from the Tamil bhakti tradition to Company trade and the Madras Presidency's law courts. The [Dravida temple architecture lecture](dravida-temple-architecture.html) is a useful companion for students before they reach the gopurams of Mylapore.

sections.h2: Historical places in Chennai by period
paras: The Parthasarathy Temple at Triplicane and the Kapaleeshwarar Temple at Mylapore are named in the hymns of the Alvars and Nayanars (roughly 6th to 9th centuries CE). The present Kapaleeshwarar buildings are much later, largely 16th century onwards, after an earlier shore temple is believed to have been lost. The Portuguese were at San Thome from the 16th century, and the tradition that St Thomas the Apostle was buried there gives the basilica its name.

Fort St George grew through the 17th and 18th centuries. St Mary's Church inside it (consecrated 1680) is the oldest Anglican church in India. The 19th century added the great public buildings: the Madras High Court (1892), the Senate House of the University of Madras (1879) and the buildings along the Marina, which mix Mughal, Deccani and Gothic features in the style called Indo-Saracenic.

sections.h2: What you see on a heritage walk in Chennai
paras: Inside Fort St George, the walk takes in St Mary's Church with its 17th and 18th century tombstones, the Fort Museum and the Secretariat, which still houses the Tamil Nadu Assembly. In George Town the street names (Armenian Street, Coral Merchant Street) record who traded there, and the Armenian Church of 1772 is a quiet courtyard in a crowded quarter.

In Mylapore the walk moves round the Kapaleeshwarar tank and through the market lanes to the temple gateway, then to San Thome Basilica (rebuilt in 1896 in neo-Gothic style). Reading the sculpture on the gopuram is easier with some background; the [lecture on reading a temple](how-to-read-a-temple.html) works well for school groups the week before.
Along the Marina, Chepauk Palace (1768, built for the Nawab of Arcot) and the Senate House show how architects such as Robert Chisholm blended Indian and European forms.

The Government Museum at Egmore, founded in 1851, is one of the oldest in India. It holds the Amaravati stupa sculptures (about the 2nd century BCE to 3rd century CE) and one of the best collections of Chola bronzes anywhere. A [museum gallery study with an archaeologist](museum-morning-with-an-archaeologist.html) is the best way to use the building with a group, because the galleries are large and labels are brief.
The Fort Museum inside Fort St George holds Company period weapons, coins, uniforms and portraits.

sections.h2: Chennai heritage walk for schools and colleges
paras: Fort St George suits younger students: it is enclosed, quieter than the city outside and tied to the arrival of European trading companies in the syllabus. Mylapore suits older students and colleges, who can discuss temples as social institutions, the tank as public space and the coexistence of temple, church and market.

Chennai walks are planned for your group, with the route and pace agreed in advance. Many groups combine the city with Mahabalipuram, about 55 km south; see our [Mamallapuram programme](mamallapuram-rock-cut-and-structural-temples.html) and the [south India temple architecture study tour](south-india-temple-architecture.html).

Chennai is hot almost all year, so start by 7.30 am and finish before noon. Fort St George is a working government complex and has security checks; carry identity documents for adults. Temples have their own dress and photography rules, and the inner sanctum may be closed to non-Hindus at some shrines. Check the ASI, museum or temple website before you go.

The three areas are several kilometres apart. Use a hired bus between them and walk within each. For the wider state, see our page on [heritage sites in Tamil Nadu](heritage-sites-in-tamil-nadu.html).

stops.name: Fort St George
stops.note: The Company's first major fort in India. Walk the ramparts' line and note how the later Secretariat sits inside the old walls.

stops.name: St Mary's Church
stops.note: Oldest Anglican church in India. Robert Clive married here; the tombstones in the yard date from the 17th century.

stops.name: Fort Museum
stops.note: Housed in a former exchange building. Look for coins, Company uniforms and a statue of Cornwallis.

stops.name: Madras High Court
stops.note: Red Indo-Saracenic court complex with domes and minarets. The old lighthouse tower stands in its grounds.

stops.name: Armenian Church
stops.note: A small church in George Town with a separate bell tower and Armenian gravestones set into the courtyard.

stops.name: George Town lanes
stops.note: The old Black Town. Street names record the trades and communities who settled here.

stops.name: Government Museum, Egmore
stops.note: Amaravati sculptures and Chola bronzes. The red Museum Theatre and the Connemara Library share the campus.

stops.name: Chepauk Palace
stops.note: Built for the Nawab of Arcot and an early example of Indo-Saracenic design. Seen from outside.

stops.name: Senate House, University of Madras
stops.note: Robert Chisholm's building mixing Byzantine and Indian forms, on the Marina.

stops.name: Parthasarathy Temple
stops.period: Origins about 8th century CE, rebuilt later
stops.note: Vaishnava temple in Triplicane praised by the Alvars. Look at the tank and the long axis to the gateway.

stops.name: Kapaleeshwarar Temple
stops.note: Shaiva temple with a tall painted gopuram and a large tank, the centre of Mylapore.

stops.name: San Thome Basilica
stops.note: Neo-Gothic church over the traditional tomb of St Thomas. A small museum explains the site's history.

stops.name: Ripon Building
stops.note: White Neoclassical home of the Greater Chennai Corporation, seen from outside near Chennai Central.

routes.name: Fort St George and George Town

museums.name: Government Museum, Egmore
museums.note: Amaravati sculpture gallery and the bronze gallery. Allow two to three hours.

museums.name: Fort Museum
museums.note: Company period objects inside Fort St George, run by the ASI.

museums.name: DakshinaChitra
museums.note: Open-air museum of south Indian houses and crafts on the road to Mahabalipuram. Needs a vehicle.

best_time: November to February. Avoid the northeast monsoon peak (late October to early December can be very wet) and plan early mornings in every season.

faq.q: What are the main historical places in Chennai?
faq.a: Fort St George with St Mary's Church, the Madras High Court, George Town, the Government Museum at Egmore, the Senate House on the Marina, and the temple towns of Mylapore and Triplicane with the Kapaleeshwarar and Parthasarathy temples.

faq.q: Which is the oldest part of Chennai?
faq.a: The temple settlements of Mylapore and Triplicane are much older than the colonial city; both are praised in Tamil devotional hymns of about the 7th to 9th centuries. The colonial city began with Fort St George in 1640.

faq.q: Can schools do a heritage walk in Chennai?
faq.a: Yes. Fort St George is the easiest for younger students because it is enclosed and less crowded. Adults need identity documents at the security check. Mylapore suits older students and colleges.

faq.q: Can I combine a Chennai walk with Mahabalipuram?
faq.a: Yes. Mahabalipuram is about 55 km south and makes a full day trip by road. Many groups spend one day in the city and one at Mahabalipuram and DakshinaChitra.

faq.q: What is special about the Government Museum in Chennai?
faq.a: It holds the Amaravati stupa sculptures and one of the largest collections of Chola bronzes in the world, along with prehistoric tools from Tamil Nadu sites such as Attirampakkam.

posts.hook: St Mary's Church in Chennai is the oldest Anglican church in India.
posts.caption: Consecrated in 1680 inside Fort St George, it still has tombstones from the 17th century. Robert Clive was married here.

posts.hook: Walk round the tank before you enter the temple.
posts.caption: At Kapaleeshwarar in Mylapore, the tank, the market and the gopuram work as one public space. Start at the steps and watch how people use them.
